_meta.deliverable: sport profiles - team field & court sports
_meta.authority_order: coach round-2 answers (COACH-R2) > round-1 answers (COACH-ANSWER) > everything else
_meta.schema: 04_profiles.json profile schema (field names kept); new fields listed in new_fields
_meta.consistency: sports the coach already covered reuse the 04 v1 weekly-set budgets unchanged or with small PROPOSED position deltas (base_profile / reuse_status on every profile); 04 numbers are not contradicted except where a newer coach round-2 rule replaces them (in-season and pre-season factors, aerobic counts)

evidence_tags.SCIENCE: external literature or official calendars, cited in references

_meta.unit: working sets per week (04 convention); athletic doses in contacts / throws / cuts / metres; conditioning in sessions per week by colour
_meta.baseline_phase: off-season build week, mid-block (04 convention); season_overrides give pre-season and in-season factors
_meta.stairway: every block climbs in gradual weekly steps (smaller early, slightly bigger after halfway, hardest weeks last); no deload or maintenance week inside a block - a block that cannot be finished is cancelled, then maintenance, then a new block (COACH-R2 PER-03/04/05, VOL-07)
_meta.check_in: no check-in = the plan follows its planned stairway (COACH-R2 VOL-03); these profiles use no lifestyle inputs (sleep / stress / job) - the coach rejected them (COACH-R2 GEN-04)
_meta.id_note: ids are new position-level ids; where a 04 variant already existed its id is kept (football_qb, basketball_guard, basketball_big, baseball_pitcher, baseball_catcher, softball_pitcher, soccer_gk, hockey_goalie, volleyball_setter, volleyball_libero)
_meta.ath02_check: ATH-02 order is kept for the ranked sports (basketball = volleyball > football skill > soccer > baseball > hockey on the plyometric dial); new sports sit by INFERRED class (rank_note)

then a chosen-length maintenance phase; at its end ask: keep maintaining / change the plan / start a training block (COACH-R2 PER-06)

in_season: Pattern: 1 match: MD+2 hard lift (>= 48 h before the next match, COACH-R2 ATH-07), MD-3 / MD-4 short power lift (04 v1 soccer). 2 matches a week: one lift on MD+2 of the first match if it is >= 48 h before the second, otherwise core / calves micro-doses only.

any_block: Mon - A1 knee + pull: warm-up -> core 2 x 2 sets, light (R2-SES-03) -> 2 plyo / ballistic -> clean variant (squat pattern, R2-ATH-04) -> HEAVY SQUAT (axial day 1, R2-SES-01) + horizontal pull -> unilateral knee-dominant (split stance) + vertical pull -> Copenhagen plank, back-extension endurance -> calves 3 sets

Tue - B1 hip + push: core 2 x 2 -> plyo + medball throws -> snatch variant (hinge pattern) -> non-axial hinge (hip thrust / back extension / reverse hyper) + horizontal push -> unilateral hip-dominant + vertical push -> hip IR / ER mobility in the warm-up -> calves 3 sets
Wed - aerobic 1 + optional Focus / core (optional days ideally separate - ORD-10)

Thu - A2 knee + pull: core 2 x 2 -> 2 plyo / ballistic -> clean variant -> leg press or belt squat (non-axial) + pull -> unilateral knee-dominant -> Copenhagen plank, back-extension endurance -> calves 3 sets

Fri - B2 hip + push: core 2 x 2 -> plyo + medball throws -> snatch variant (hinge pattern) -> HEAVY DEADLIFT / trap-bar (axial day 2, R2-SES-01) + push -> unilateral hip-dominant -> hip IR / ER mobility in the warm-up -> calves 3 sets
Sat - aerobic 2 + aerobic 3 (or after a lifting day)
Sun - off

rules: limit loaded deep hip flexion volume (box squats to parallel)
hip IR/ER mobility in warm-up
more UHD than deep BKD
'Coppenhaggen Plank' (R47 / O165) 3x/week pre-season, 1-2x/week in-season
adductor-integrated chops / Pallofs ('Hold object Adducted between knees'); banded adduction variants are out of scope (no bands, EQ-01 / EQ-07)
frontal / transverse unilateral work (lateral lunges, cossacks, lateral step-ups) - UNI-12
prefer DB/KB neutral grips over front-rack barbell for strikers
limit front-squat rack volume when wrist pain flagged
add ISO_NECK 2x/week (isometric 4-way, then plate or manual eccentric; no bands - EQ-01) - NO library column exists: create one
progress static -> dynamic like the core plane ladder
COACH-ANSWER VOL-03: cut that muscle or pattern 30-50%, move it to machines or split grips, keep it moving - or drop the exercise altogether if it is too much

swap fixed-grip barbell/bar -> DB/KB/handles in the same pattern; swap bilateral -> unilateral in the same pattern (MASTER_MODEL athletic A6); keep the sets ideally, 'but you have to adjust accordingly' (UNI-08)
pain moves the bilateral : unilateral share (UNI-02)
all prehab uses DB, KB, cable, machine, bodyweight or plates - never bands or variable resistance (COACH-ANSWER EQ-01, EQ-12)

age_notes: high school, college and pro: same plan; loads and speeds change, pros get more care for their bodies (COACH-ANSWER PRG-09)
youth: Olympic lifts from the floor from about 14, after one block of hang work; growth-spurt / younger athletes use youth_athlete (COACH-R2 ATH-08, ATH-09)

60+: no Olympic lifts, plyos or depth jumps by default; offered as an option with 'Make sure that you have a fitness professional to help you understand what this means' (COACH-R2 ATH-08); constrained machines for compounds and isolation (EQ-03)
more than 6-12 months off: the body is treated as L1 (PRG-05)
no rule depends on sex (ATH-09)

off_season: Mon - A1 knee + pull: warm-up -> core 2 x 2 sets, light (R2-SES-03) -> 2 plyo / ballistic -> clean variant (squat pattern, R2-ATH-04) -> HEAVY SQUAT (axial day 1, R2-SES-01) + horizontal pull -> unilateral knee-dominant (contralateral load) + vertical pull -> Copenhagen plank, neck isometrics 4-way -> calves 3 sets

Tue - B1 hip + push: speed / COD block first (squirrel jumps -> MACH / acceleration starts -> max velocity, LIB-21; route tree EASY -> MOD. -> HARD TURN, ATH-06) -> core 2 x 2 -> plyo + medball throws -> snatch variant (hinge pattern) -> non-axial hinge (hip thrust / back extension / reverse hyper) + horizontal push -> unilateral hip-dominant + vertical push -> wrist / forearm, hip IR / ER mobility in the warm-up -> calves 3 sets
Wed - aerobic 1 + optional Focus / core (optional days ideally separate - ORD-10)

Thu - A2 knee + pull: core 2 x 2 -> 2 plyo / ballistic -> clean variant -> leg press or belt squat (non-axial) + pull -> unilateral knee-dominant -> Copenhagen plank, neck isometrics 4-way -> calves 3 sets

Fri - B2 hip + push: speed / COD block first (squirrel jumps -> MACH / acceleration starts -> max velocity, LIB-21; route tree EASY -> MOD. -> HARD TURN, ATH-06) -> core 2 x 2 -> plyo + medball throws -> snatch variant (hinge pattern) -> HEAVY DEADLIFT / trap-bar (axial day 2, R2-SES-01) + push -> unilateral hip-dominant -> wrist / forearm, hip IR / ER mobility in the warm-up -> calves 3 sets
Sat - aerobic 2 + aerobic 3 (or after a lifting day)
Sun - off
pre_season: Mon: speed / COD block first (squirrel jumps -> MACH / acceleration starts -> max velocity, LIB-21; route tree EASY -> MOD. -> HARD TURN, ATH-06) -> core 2 x 2 -> plyo (stage held) -> clean variant (heavier, fewer sets) -> HEAVY SQUAT 3-5 reps, fast intent (axial day 1) + pull -> unilateral -> calves
Wed: core 2 x 2 -> plyo + medball throws -> snatch variant (hinge pattern) -> belt squat / hip thrust (non-axial) + push -> unilateral -> Copenhagen plank, neck isometrics 4-way

Fri: speed / COD block first (squirrel jumps -> MACH / acceleration starts -> max velocity, LIB-21; route tree EASY -> MOD. -> HARD TURN, ATH-06) -> core 2 x 2 -> plyo -> clean or snatch -> HEAVY DEADLIFT / trap bar (axial day 2) + pull -> wrist / forearm, hip IR / ER mobility in the warm-up -> calves
Tue / Thu / Sat: team practice; aerobic 2 = 1 Blue sport-specific repeat-effort session + 1 Green
about 60 % of the off-season weekly sets (target about 60 %, COACH-R2 PER-06); last 1-2 weeks = taper (volume -40-60 %, intensity kept, no new exercises)
in_season: Pattern: 1-2 games a week: MD+2 hard lift >= 48 h before the next game; MD-3 short power lift (as soccer).

Hard lift (>= 48 h before the next game, R2-ATH-07): core 2 x 2 -> 1 plyo at about half volume -> Olympic light 2 x 3 -> squat OR deadlift (alternate weeks; 3-5 reps, RIR 2-3; bilateral kept minimal - UNI-10) + pull -> 1 unilateral -> Copenhagen plank, neck isometrics 4-way -> calves
Short lift (mid-week): core 2 x 2 -> unilateral + upper push / pull 2 sets -> wrist / forearm, hip IR / ER mobility in the warm-up
Day after a game: Orange flush 20-30 min + mobility; game days: no lifting
Aerobic: 2 a week in season (COACH-ANSWER ATH-07) - usually the post-game Orange flush + 1 short Blue / Green if game minutes are low
post_season: 1-2 weeks: arm care / mobility / easy Orange cardio, no athletic work (04 post_season_recovery)
then a chosen-length maintenance phase; at its end ask: keep maintaining / change the plan / start a training block (COACH-R2 PER-06)
rules: power before strength; horizontal pull before vertical (ORD-01..03); hip-dominant with push, knee-dominant with pull (UNI-11)
up to 12 exercises + the 2-exercise core block (R2-SES-04); muscles trained that day get 2-4 exercises (R2-SES-05 - see open question O2)
every week a step up the stairway; no deload or maintenance week inside the block (R2-PER-03/04, R2-VOL-07)
aerobic colours: A + B + C - one of each colour (cheat-sheet rule, OBSERVED; COACH-ANSWER ATH-07) (A = Blue (short / high), B = Green (1-3 min), C = Orange (long / low), LC = lactate clearance)

Wed: core 2 x 2 -> plyo + medball throws -> snatch variant (hinge pattern) -> belt squat / hip thrust (non-axial) + push -> unilateral -> Nordic / slider curls

Fri: speed / COD block first (squirrel jumps -> MACH / acceleration starts -> max velocity, LIB-21; route tree EASY -> MOD. -> HARD TURN, ATH-06) -> core 2 x 2 -> plyo -> clean or snatch -> HEAVY DEADLIFT / trap bar (axial day 2) + pull -> Copenhagen plank + rear delts (own sets) -> calves
Tue / Thu / Sat: team practice; aerobic 2 = 1 Blue sport-specific repeat-effort session + 1 Green
about 65 % of the off-season weekly sets (target about 60 %, COACH-R2 PER-06); last 1-2 weeks = taper (volume -40-60 %, intensity kept, no new exercises)
in_season: Pattern: weekend tournaments: Mon recovery + Orange flush, Tue hard lift (>= 48 h before Saturday), Thu short power lift or off.

Hard lift (>= 48 h before the next game, R2-ATH-07): core 2 x 2 -> 1 plyo at about half volume -> Olympic light 2 x 3 -> squat OR deadlift (alternate weeks; 3-5 reps, RIR 2-3; bilateral kept minimal - UNI-10) + pull -> 1 unilateral -> Nordic / slider curls -> calves
Short lift (mid-week): core 2 x 2 -> 1 max-velocity sprint exposure (speed athlete) -> unilateral + upper push / pull 2 sets -> Copenhagen plank + rear delts (own sets)
Day after a game: Orange flush 20-30 min + mobility; game days: no lifting

post_season: 1-2 weeks: arm care / mobility / easy Orange cardio, no athletic work (04 post_season_recovery)
then a chosen-length maintenance phase; at its end ask: keep maintaining / change the plan / start a training block (COACH-R2 PER-06)
rules: power before strength; horizontal pull before vertical (ORD-01..03); hip-dominant with push, knee-dominant with pull (UNI-11)
up to 12 exercises + the 2-exercise core block (R2-SES-04); muscles trained that day get 2-4 exercises (R2-SES-05 - see open question O2)
every week a step up the stairway; no deload or maintenance week inside the block (R2-PER-03/04, R2-VOL-07)

open_questions.topic: Floor of 10 weekly sets per muscle vs athlete budgets
open_questions.detail: COACH-R2 VOL-04/06: 'I don't think anybody needs less than 10 sets a week per muscle.' The 04 athlete budgets reused here give field athletes far fewer direct upper-body sets (e.g. soccer chest about 2-4). Proposed reading: the floor applies to muscles the athlete's plan trains for size / strength in the off-season; pre-season (about 60 %) and in-season blocks are maintenance phases and may sit below 10. Needs the coach's yes.
open_questions.status: OPEN - flag to the volume engine owner

open_questions.topic: 2-4 exercises per muscle on full-body days vs the 12 + 2 cap
open_questions.detail: COACH-R2 SES-05 (2-4 exercises per muscle on full-body days, never 1) and COACH-R2 SES-04 (field athletes up to 12 exercises + 2 core) collide on athletic full-body days that already hold 4-6 athletic exercises. Proposed: 2-4 exercises for each muscle TRAINED that day (knee + pull day / hip + push day pairing), not for every muscle; athletic exercises do not count toward the cap's resistance part.

open_questions.topic: Sports not on the coach's approved lists
open_questions.detail: COACH-R2 ATH-01 (plyo share by class) and ATH-06 (aerobic sessions) named basketball, volleyball, soccer, football, baseball, softball and hockey. Lacrosse, field hockey, rugby, cheer / STUNT, ultimate, flag and beach volleyball use INFERRED classes and PROPOSED aerobic counts. COACH-R2 ATH-07 (game-heavy in-season reductions) is extended to lacrosse, field hockey, rugby, ultimate, flag, beach and cheer by analogy.

COACH-R2 ATH-07 says in-season sprints only for speed athletes; the 04 HAMSTRING rule keeps one max-velocity exposure a week in every phase. Resolved here as: games supply it; athletes with few game minutes keep one exposure (INFERRED). Basketball guards are no longer given in-season sprints (04 v1 INFERRED content superseded).

Not on the ATH-07 game-heavy list. The coach's OBSERVED Block 3 kept 4 days at 4 x 10 with no Olympic lifts; PER-08 says about 2 lifting days, and COACH-R2 ATH-04 approves a light Olympic piece in season. Profiles use 2 days + the light piece; the 4-day observed version stays evidence.

GEN-02 gives recreational players no season. Many rec players have a fixed weekly game. Proposed: an optional 'league game day' input that keeps the hardest lower-body day >= 48 h away and swaps one aerobic session for the game.
Indoor volleyball is class 2 (60 %, COACH-R2 ATH-01). Sand slows the take-off (T20), so beach is set to class 3 (50 %) - PROPOSED.
Neck isometrics added for lacrosse, field hockey, rugby, cheer, flag and soccer defenders on the concussion / neck-strength evidence (T38). The library still has no neck column (04 library gap).

All name_es values are drafts in neutral Latin American Spanish with English terms in brackets; the coach (or a coach he trusts) approves every line (COACH-R2 GEN-08). 'Cheerleading (porrismo)' and the field-hockey / lacrosse terms especially need a check.

Rugby sevens: high-intensity intermittent running + contact, about 6 matches over 2-3 days per tournament
US cheerleading: stunts cause about 60% of injuries and 96% of concussions / closed head injuries; bases and spotters most often injured; ankle, low back and wrist re-injured most
Cheer pop-off dismount landings: 2.1-14.9 body weights (flyers about 6 BW)
Tumbling take-off contact about 120-130 ms (double back somersault, World Championships); back handspring take-off about 0.13-0.18 s
STUNT (head-to-head competitive cheer): spring season (first contest Feb 1), NCAA championship sport from spring 2027
Competitive ultimate (GPS): 4.7 km per game, 0.63 km high-intensity, 0.21 km sprinting, 17 sprints, mean HR 82% / peak 99% HRmax (Krustrup & Mohr 2015)
Ultimate injuries: muscle strains 76%, ankle 65%, knee 53%, shoulder 37%, head 30% of players; 49% recurrent (Reynolds & Halsmer 2006)
Beach volleyball: 52-85 jumps per player per match, rallies about 8.5 s, blockers jump most (systematic review)
Jumping on sand vs a rigid surface: lower jump height and longer time to reach peak take-off velocity
Beach vs indoor volleyball: similar external load, more small (<20 cm) jumps and higher heart-rate load on sand
Pro ice hockey: defensemen more time on ice (16:35 vs 14:39) and more decelerations; forwards more high-intensity work per minute
Butterfly goalies: high prevalence of symptomatic FAI (cam deformity) vs skaters
Ice hockey skating: blade contact per stride shortens with speed but stays long (about 0.6 s at fast speed, ISBS proceedings)
Soccer positions: central midfielders the most total distance, wide midfielders and full-backs the most high-speed running, centre-backs the least (but many accelerations)
Soccer goalkeepers: about 50% of outfield total distance and 10% of high-intensity distance; dives and explosive efforts rise late in matches
Change of direction: ground contact time rises with cut angle (45 < 90 < 180 degrees); 45-degree cuts about 0.16-0.24 s
Basketball positions: guards more distance, accelerations and decelerations; forwards more high-speed running; centres more jumps and rebounds (scoping review)
NCAA football injuries 2014-19: 9.31 / 1000 AE; concussion 7.5%, ankle sprain 6.9%, hamstring 4.7%; blocking and tackling common mechanisms
NFL quarterbacks: shoulder 15.2% of injuries (AC sprains about 40% of them); overuse = rotator cuff / biceps tendinitis
Baseball catcher squat biomechanics (relaxed / ready stance, throw to second): repeated deep knee flexion
